exposure: pelvic diameters (interspinous, intertrochanteric, intercristal, external conjugate, Anterior Pelvic Index)
outcome: delivery outcomes (spontaneous vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: 108 pregnant women in the active phase of labor who were admitted to the Gynecological Clinic at the Clinical Center University of Sarajevo.
finding: Maternal age, BMI, and pelvic diameters are significant determinants of delivery outcomes, suggesting their importance in personalized delivery care.
mod_finding: Women undergoing cesarean section were significantly older than those with spontaneous vaginal delivery, and maternal age and BMI significantly correlated with delivery outcomes.
cross-section timing: During the active phase of labor upon admission.
